analysis_notes.speaker: Ross Tucker
analysis_notes.topic: DeMico Ryans defensive play-calling
analysis_notes.summary: DeMico Ryans took defensive play-calling back from DC Matt Burke following communication breakdowns in coverage.
analysis_notes.quote: DeMico Ryans is taking defensive play calling back from Matt Burke.

analysis_notes.show: Ross Tucker — Greg Cosell's Week 5 Preview Part 2
analysis_notes.speaker: Greg Cosell
analysis_notes.topic: Cam Ward mechanics and Titans running back room
analysis_notes.summary: Cam Ward needs significant work on dropback footwork and pocket setting, causing erratic ball placement on routine throws; Tony Pollard is better suited in a tandem than as a true feature back.
analysis_notes.quote: He still needs so much work with his footwork on his drop and set in the pocket... he's just so unsettled.

analysis_notes.show: Ross Tucker — Greg Cosell's Week 5 Preview Part 2
analysis_notes.speaker: Greg Cosell
analysis_notes.topic: Arvell Reese rookie performance and pass rush usage
analysis_notes.summary: Arvell Reese has performed as a dominant second-level defender through four games and is receiving increased third-down pass-rush snaps in NASCAR fronts following Brian Burns' injury.
analysis_notes.quote: He has been a dominant second-level defender through four games.

analysis_notes.show: Ross Tucker — Greg Cosell's Week 5 Preview Part 2
analysis_notes.speaker: Greg Cosell
analysis_notes.topic: Ben Johnson Bears run scheme design
analysis_notes.summary: Ben Johnson's creative run scheme using shifts, motions, and heavy formations leverages elite run blocking on the right side of the O-line from Darnell Wright and Jonah Jackson.
analysis_notes.quote: Ben Johnson is the one who puts together the run game... he is a master at it with his use of formations, shifts, and motions.

analysis_notes.show: Ross Tucker — Greg Cosell's Week 5 Preview Part 2
analysis_notes.speaker: Greg Cosell
analysis_notes.topic: Bo Nix struggles against 5 and 6 man blitzes
analysis_notes.summary: Bo Nix is completing just 34.8% (16 of 46) against 5- and 6-man pressures through four games, making blitzes a primary key for opponent gameplans.
analysis_notes.quote: Against 5 and 6 man pressures through the first four games, Bo Nix is 16 for 46. That's 34.8%.

analysis_notes.show: Ross Tucker — Greg Cosell's Week 5 Preview Part 2
analysis_notes.speaker: Greg Cosell
analysis_notes.topic: Justin Herbert scheme fit in quick-timing offenses
analysis_notes.summary: Herbert's physical skill set favors deep-drop, downfield passing concepts (Coryell/Martz style) rather than quick-timing, compact-delivery offenses like Mike McDaniel's system.
analysis_notes.quote: I don't know if Herbert is that twitchy, sudden guy that fits that quick timing, get the ball out, compact delivery offense.

analysis_notes.show: Ross Tucker — Greg Cosell's Week 5 Preview Part 2
analysis_notes.speaker: Greg Cosell
analysis_notes.topic: Lions passing offense vs secondary coverage issues
analysis_notes.summary: Jared Goff executes the Lions pass game efficiently from the pocket, but Detroit's defense struggles when forced into zone coverage, missing key safety Brian Branch.
analysis_notes.quote: Jared Goff is probably one of those really good quarterbacks that's overlooked a lot because he doesn't run around.

analysis_notes.show: Ross Tucker — Greg Cosell's Week 5 Preview Part 2
analysis_notes.speaker: Greg Cosell
analysis_notes.topic: Cardinals offensive volume and key playmakers
analysis_notes.summary: Jeremiah Love needs to be the central centerpiece of Arizona's run game, while Michael Wilson continues to stand out as a high-caliber starting receiver.
analysis_notes.quote: I think he has to become the foundation of the offense. I think it has to start with Jeremiah Love and run through him.

analysis_notes.show: Ross Tucker — Greg Cosell's Week 5 Preview Part 2
analysis_notes.speaker: Greg Cosell
analysis_notes.topic: Brock Purdy post-snap processing and operational efficiency
analysis_notes.summary: Brock Purdy operates San Francisco's offense at an elite level through discipline, quick post-snap processing, and ball placement despite lacking a top-tier arm.
analysis_notes.quote: He is an elite post-snap operator... he knows how to play the quarterback position with all the details and nuance.

analysis_notes.show: Ross Tucker — Greg Cosell's Week 5 Preview Part 2
analysis_notes.speaker: Greg Cosell
analysis_notes.topic: Falcons play-action efficiency paired with outside zone
analysis_notes.summary: Michael Penix Jr. is 12 of 16 for 236 yards on play-action over his last two games, effective because Bijan Robinson's outside zone forces lateral steps from defensive line and linebackers.
analysis_notes.quote: In the play action pass game the last two weeks, Penix is 12 for 16 for 236.

analysis_notes.show: Ross Tucker — Greg Cosell's Week 5 Preview Part 2
analysis_notes.speaker: Greg Cosell
analysis_notes.topic: Dalton Kincaid involvement in Joe Brady pass scheme
analysis_notes.summary: Bills offensive coordinator Joe Brady needs to design targeted looks for Dalton Kincaid, as Buffalo lacks elite perimeter wideouts and needs Kincaid as a primary pass catcher.
analysis_notes.quote: You have got to find a way to get Dalton Kincaid involved in your pass game.

analysis_notes.show: Ross Tucker — Greg Cosell's Week 5 Preview Part 2
analysis_notes.speaker: Ross Tucker
analysis_notes.topic: Buccaneers TNF upset over Cowboys
analysis_notes.summary: Buccaneers secured a TNF victory over Dallas behind big plays from Bucky Irving and Tez Johnson, sealed by Alex Anzalone's late interception against a struggling Cowboys defense.
analysis_notes.quote: There was a massive win for the Bucs on Thursday Night Football... huge upset over the Dallas Cowboys.

analysis_notes.show: Ross Tucker — Greg Cosell's Week 5 Preview Part 1
analysis_notes.speaker: Greg Cosell
analysis_notes.topic: Lane Johnson retirement & signature technique
analysis_notes.summary: Greg Cosell evaluates Lane Johnson as one of the greatest right tackles in NFL history, highlighting his signature double-under pass protection move developed against Brandon Graham during practice.
analysis_notes.quote: I'm not sure we've seen a better right tackle than Lane Johnson... that double-under pass protection move... he developed that against Brandon Graham in practice.

analysis_notes.show: Ross Tucker — Greg Cosell's Week 5 Preview Part 1
analysis_notes.speaker: Greg Cosell
analysis_notes.topic: Jalon Daniels QB progression and Cowboys secondary alignment
analysis_notes.summary: Greg Cosell highlights Jalon Daniels' timing, anticipation, and progression reading. On defense, Dallas shifted Caleb Downs from slot to true safety, putting Stewart in the slot while re-evaluating outside corner roles with DaRon Bland.
analysis_notes.quote: He showed at Kansas that he knew how to play the quarterback position... he had a sense of timing and anticipation that he could progression read.

analysis_notes.show: Ross Tucker — Greg Cosell's Week 5 Preview Part 1
analysis_notes.speaker: Greg Cosell
analysis_notes.topic: Eagles third down blitz vulnerability vs Jaguars pressure
analysis_notes.summary: Eagles struggle against extra pressure, going 0-for-12 on third downs last week when facing 5+ rushers. Jaguars DC Anthony Campanile presents a significant test with his aggressive blitz schemes.
analysis_notes.quote: All eight of those Hurts dropbacks on third down, the Rams rushed five or more... and they did not have an answer.

analysis_notes.show: Ross Tucker — Greg Cosell's Week 5 Preview Part 1
analysis_notes.speaker: Greg Cosell
analysis_notes.topic: Bengals pass-heavy offense imbalance
analysis_notes.summary: Bengals offense is overly reliant on Joe Burrow's arm, ranking second-lowest in rushing attempts and yards despite having Chase Brown, creating a reactive strain on the offensive line.
analysis_notes.quote: They've got the second fewest rushing attempts of any team in the league and the second fewest rushing yards.

analysis_notes.show: Ross Tucker — Greg Cosell's Week 5 Preview Part 1
analysis_notes.speaker: Greg Cosell
analysis_notes.topic: Raiders heavy personnel reliance with Brock Bowers
analysis_notes.summary: Raiders ran 11 personnel (3 WRs) on just 7 total snaps over two games with Brock Bowers back, leaning heavily into 12, 13, and 21 sets. Patriots offense responded by utilizing 6 O-linemen to handle Maxx Crosby.
analysis_notes.quote: You know how many snaps in these two games they played with three wide receivers on the field? Seven.

analysis_notes.show: Ross Tucker — Greg Cosell's Week 5 Preview Part 1
analysis_notes.speaker: Greg Cosell
analysis_notes.topic: Vikings Brian Flores base defense pressure scheme
analysis_notes.summary: Brian Flores runs a unique defense that brings 5+ rushers on over 70% of dropbacks directly out of base personnel, relying on zone match principles behind the blitz.
analysis_notes.quote: They've been rushing five or more literally on 70% of quarterback dropbacks out of base.

analysis_notes.show: Ross Tucker — Greg Cosell's Week 5 Preview Part 1
analysis_notes.speaker: Greg Cosell
analysis_notes.topic: Browns dominant man defense vs Jets historic low play volume
analysis_notes.summary: Browns play the highest rate of single-high man coverage with an aggressive secondary. The Jets offense managed a historic low 32 total offensive plays last week (4 in Q1, 2 in Q4).
analysis_notes.quote: The Jets ran 32 offensive plays, Ross, this past week... they ran four plays in the first quarter and two plays in the fourth quarter.

analysis_notes.show: Ross Tucker — Greg Cosell's Week 5 Preview Part 1
analysis_notes.speaker: Greg Cosell
analysis_notes.topic: Steelers offensive identity through Jaylen Warren and TEs
analysis_notes.summary: Greg Cosell argues Jaylen Warren is the Steelers' top offensive weapon and should be featured with 20+ touches, advising Pittsburgh to throw inside to tight ends rather than forcing outside 1-on-1s.
analysis_notes.quote: When I watch the Steelers, I always come away feeling that Jaylen Warren is their best player on offense.

analysis_notes.show: Ross Tucker — Greg Cosell's Week 5 Preview Part 1
analysis_notes.speaker: Ross Tucker
analysis_notes.topic: Ravens acquire Cam Jurgens in trade with Eagles
analysis_notes.summary: Eagles trade interior offensive lineman Cam Jurgens to Baltimore for 2nd and 5th round picks. Ravens bolster center position for a playoff push while Eagles gain draft capital and cap relief.
analysis_notes.quote: The Ravens recognize that they have a window here including this year to do something special.

analysis_notes.speaker: Producer Jack
analysis_notes.topic: DeMeco Ryans reassumes defensive play-calling; Tank Dell IR return
analysis_notes.summary: Houston Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans takes back defensive play-calling duties from DC Matt Burke, while wide receiver Tank Dell is designated to return from IR.
analysis_notes.quote: Head coach DeMeco Ryans taking over defensive play calling from defensive coordinator Matt Burke.
